title: P versus PSPACE
formal: Does every language decidable by a deterministic Turing machine using polynomial working space have a deterministic polynomial-time decision algorithm? Equivalently, do there exist a machine A and constants C,k such that A decides truth of every closed quantified Boolean formula of encoded length n in at most $C(n+1)^k$ steps?
definitions: P consists of languages decided by one deterministic multitape Turing machine with a fixed polynomial worst-case time bound. PSPACE consists of languages decided by one deterministic Turing machine which halts on every input and visits at most \(C(n+1)^{k}\) work-tape cells, for some constants C,k, on inputs of length n. The input is read-only and is not charged as work space; a fixed finite tape alphabet is used. PSPACE imposes no polynomial time bound. A closed quantified Boolean formula has the form \(Q_{1}x_{1}\cdots Q_{m}x_{m} \varphi (x_{1},\ldots ,x_{m})\), where each \(Q_{i}\) is \(\exists\) or \(\forall\), quantified variables are distinct, and \(\varphi\) is an explicitly encoded Boolean formula using AND, OR, and NOT, with no free variables. Every quantifier ranges over \(\{0,1\}\). The number of quantifiers and their alternations may grow with n; the input is not restricted to a fixed number of blocks. Use any standard explicit binary encoding, reject malformed inputs, and count its full bit length n. Truth means the usual nested Boolean quantifier semantics. This language, TQBF, is PSPACE-complete under polynomial-time many-one reductions. No oracle, advice, randomization, or promise is allowed. In this statement, “explicitly given/encoded/listed” means the entire finite list, table or syntax tree described above is part of the input or output, with its full encoding counted; it does not mean a circuit, oracle or program generating a larger object.
answer_criterion: Prove \(\mathrm{P}=\mathrm{PSPACE}\) or \(\mathrm{P}\ne \mathrm{PSPACE}\). The first outcome asserts a deterministic polynomial-time decision procedure for every polynomial-space language; the second asserts a polynomial-space language with no deterministic polynomial-time decision procedure.
why: This asks whether reusing a feasible amount of memory can provide computational power beyond feasible running time. It is a central unresolved separation even when the allowed language class is enlarged from NP to all of PSPACE, and it organizes the complexity of quantified reasoning, games, and verification.

importance.reason: A defining question about the relationship between the two basic computational resources, time and working memory. It is a top-priority foundational class separation.

progress.text: Quantified Boolean formulas provide a PSPACE-complete target. Chandra, Kozen, and Stockmeyer characterize deterministic polynomial space as alternating polynomial time.
Shamir proves \(\mathrm{IP}=\mathrm{PSPACE}\), giving an interactive-proof characterization without resolving deterministic polynomial-time computation.

Williams proves the \(O(\sqrt{t \log  t})\) space simulation of time-t multitape machines, improving the decades-old \(O(t/\log  t)\) bound. It yields fixed-exponent time lower bounds for linear-space languages.
Williams’ MFCS invited survey discusses this simulation and further space-complexity developments. It supplies no separation of the unions P and PSPACE.

status_note: Primary-source review and a search for subsequent results on 11 September 2026 found no resolution. Williams’ 2025 simulation and August 2026 MFCS survey concern time-space bounds; neither states an equality or separation of P and PSPACE.

context_blocks.text: Time measures the total number of computation steps; space measures how much information the machine retains at once. Space can be reused. For example, a machine can evaluate a quantified formula by recursively exploring possible choices and reusing its work area when it returns from a branch. The resulting computation may inspect exponentially many choices while keeping only a polynomial amount of information.

Alternating quantifiers express a finite game of choices: existential moves try to make the final formula true, and universal moves challenge them. For example, \(\forall x\exists y (y=x)\) is true because y may depend on x, whereas \(\exists y\forall x (y=x)\) is false. Both variables range over \(\{0,1\}\). A winning strategy for a longer formula can have exponentially many branches even though each play has polynomial length. Polynomial-time alternation captures exactly PSPACE.

The inclusion \(\mathrm{P}\subseteq \mathrm{PSPACE}\) is immediate, but its strictness is unknown. \(\mathrm{P}\ne \mathrm{NP}\) would imply \(\mathrm{P}\ne \mathrm{PSPACE}\) because \(\mathrm{NP}\subseteq \mathrm{PSPACE}\). A proof of \(\mathrm{P}=\mathrm{NP}\), however, would collapse the polynomial hierarchy without automatically giving a polynomial-time algorithm for formulas with an unbounded number of quantifier alternations. This separates the present question from merely solving satisfiability.

The theorem \(\mathrm{IP}=\mathrm{PSPACE}\) characterizes the same space class through interaction: a polynomial-time randomized verifier can check claims from an unbounded prover using a bounded-error interactive protocol. The prover’s assistance is a resource. Removing the prover to obtain an ordinary deterministic polynomial-time algorithm is not a consequence of that characterization.

Williams’ time-to-space simulation gives a concrete advance in the comparison of these resources. For time bounds \(t(n)\ge n, a\) time-t multitape computation can be simulated in \(O(\sqrt{t \log  t})\) working space. A consequence is that some linear-space languages require time \(n^{2- \varepsilon}\) for every \(\varepsilon >0\). The lower-bound exponent remains bounded: the result does not exhibit a polynomial-space language outside every polynomial time bound.

sentences: Polynomial space permits a computation to reuse its memory while exploring potentially enormous collections of possibilities.
The question asks whether every problem solvable with that memory budget is also solvable in polynomial time.
Truth of quantified Boolean formulas supplies a concrete complete problem.
Alternating existential and universal choices describe strategies that can be much larger than one ordinary certificate.
The project tests whether repeated reuse of a modest workspace gives strictly more decision power than any polynomial-time computation.
